checks.statement: Support a left-side sheet with reversed elements for RTL languages. M3 modal side sheets use a 16dp corner radius and updated color mappings compatible with dynamic color.
checks.condition: When applying M3 side-sheet styling and RTL placement.

sourceHistory.summary: M2 comparison names RTL support and modal-sheet radius and color changes.

evidence.result: CSS supports start-side orientation and reverses corner assignments, while modal shape comes from token-bound radii; no locale binding demonstrates automatic RTL mirroring.

implementation.notes: The orientation must be set by caller and was not verified against RTL locale direction.

checks.statement: Use 24dp start/end padding, 12dp between top elements, 72dp bottom actions height with 16dp top and 24dp bottom padding, left-aligned bottom actions, 400dp maximum width, and 16dp margins when detached.
checks.condition: When sizing and laying out a standard side sheet.

sourceHistory.summary: Standard measurements table gives padding, actions, max width, and detached margins.

evidence.result: Sheet header/body/footer use token-bound spacing, width and action variables; this code inspection does not establish resolved 24dp/12dp/72dp/400dp values for the standard variant.

checks.statement: Use 24dp start/end padding, 16dp start padding when a back icon is present, 12dp between top elements, 72dp bottom actions height with 16dp top and 24dp bottom padding, left-aligned actions, 400dp maximum width, and 16dp detached margins.
checks.condition: When sizing and laying out a modal side sheet.

sourceHistory.summary: Modal measurements table gives padding, icon-specific padding, actions, max width, and detached margins.

evidence.result: The modal uses the same sheet layout slots with token-bound spacing and width variables, but the modal back-icon conditional padding and resolved dimensions were not verified.

implementation.notes: The specimen omits a back icon, so its conditional 16dp start padding is not exercised.

checks.statement: Use side sheets to provide optional content and actions without interrupting access to primary content. Use standard sheets mainly at medium and expanded breakpoints for supplementary content and contextual actions while primary content remains interactive; use modal sheets preferably at compact breakpoints, where they must be dismissed before interacting with underlying content. Side sheets have fixed width, typically span screen height, and should sit at a screen edge, usually on the right, with at most a 16dp inset.
checks.condition: When choosing a side-sheet variant and placement for a window size.

sourceHistory.summary: Usage guidance distinguishes standard and modal use by breakpoint, interaction model, and placement.

implementation.notes: Selecting standard versus modal by breakpoint is an application integration decision; the specimen exposes the variants but does not implement responsive product selection.

checks.statement: The container is the only required element of a side sheet; its size is determined by the elements it holds.

sourceHistory.summary: Container guidance names the only required element and how its size is determined.

evidence.result: The side sheet is represented by a container whose content is nested and optional; the sheet element itself exists without any requirement that each optional slot be populated.

checks.statement: A back icon button may let people leave the side sheet or move to another experience; provide an affordance for returning to primary content because that content remains visible beside or behind the sheet.
checks.condition: When a side sheet supports navigation or needs an explicit return path.

sourceHistory.summary: Back-button guidance describes optional navigation and the need to return to visible primary content.

implementation.notes: The side-sheet example does not implement a back-navigation flow or nested experience; the back affordance is optional when such navigation exists.

checks.statement: Provide a close affordance; a close icon button is highly recommended because it gives a consistent dismissal method, improves accessibility, and makes focused sheets easier to close.
checks.condition: For a side sheet that can be dismissed.

sourceHistory.summary: Close-button guidance strongly recommends an explicit close affordance and states its benefits.

evidence.result: The sheet content includes a labeled close button wired to the close action.

checks.statement: Use action buttons for actions available from the sheet, such as Save, Edit, or Download; use elevation, fill, and tone to draw attention to specific actions.
checks.condition: When a side sheet presents actions.

sourceHistory.summary: Action-button guidance gives use and emphasis treatments.

evidence.result: The footer exposes two text actions and the side-sheet action class receives its component styling.

checks.statement: Use a divider to separate distinct content regions, including actions from content or user-generated content from system-generated content.
checks.condition: When a side sheet contains content that benefits from a visual separation.

sourceHistory.summary: Divider guidance identifies two separations for which dividers should be used.

evidence.result: Docked standard side sheets use a token-bound divider at the inline edge between sheet and primary content.

checks.statement: Side sheets may contain varied content and layouts, including action lists, supplemental content, and tabular layouts. A modal sheet may transition to a standard sheet on a larger screen.
checks.condition: When selecting content or adapting a modal side sheet to a larger screen.

sourceHistory.summary: Content guidance permits varied layouts and describes modal-to-standard adaptation.

evidence.result: The content slot includes body content and footer actions; the container itself allows caller-provided content, but no responsive modal-to-standard transition is implemented.

checks.statement: Resize the default side-sheet width as layout needs require. When a standard side sheet opens, shrink the body area to accommodate it while maintaining a margin on the body's trailing edge.
checks.condition: When a standard side sheet opens or its layout adapts.

sourceHistory.summary: Adaptive guidance describes width flexibility and body-area adjustment.

evidence.result: The side sheet is absolutely positioned at a fixed token width; the frame/page content is not resized or given a trailing margin when a standard sheet opens.

checks.statement: For right-to-left languages, place side sheets on the left edge of the window and reverse all sheet elements.
checks.condition: When the interface uses a right-to-left language.

sourceHistory.summary: RTL guidance specifies left-edge placement and reversal of sheet elements.

evidence.result: A caller-selected start orientation moves the sheet to the start edge and reverses corners, but no code derives that orientation from RTL direction.

implementation.notes: Locale-driven RTL placement is not demonstrated.

checks.statement: Allow a side sheet to scroll vertically independent of the rest of the UI so its scroll position and the page's position can persist independently; do not allow or suggest horizontal scrolling.
checks.condition: When side-sheet content exceeds the available height or is scrollable.

sourceHistory.summary: Behavior guidance permits independent vertical scrolling and prohibits horizontal scrolling.

evidence.result: Sheet content is overflow-hidden and the body has no independent vertical overflow rule; oversized content cannot scroll inside the sheet.

checks.statement: On Android predictive back, detach the sheet from the top and bottom screen edges, preview the previous screen, and scale the sheet and its content in the gesture direction.
checks.condition: When implementing Android predictive back for side sheets.

sourceHistory.summary: Predictive-back guidance lists detachment, previous-screen preview, and gesture-direction scaling.

implementation.notes: Android predictive-back preview/scale is a platform integration effect; this implementation is web-only.

checks.statement: People must be able to dismiss a side sheet using assistive technology.

sourceHistory.summary: Use cases require dismissal through assistive technology.

evidence.result: The close button and native dialog cancel event call close(), and standard modal/outside interactions also close the sheet.

checks.statement: Always provide a close affordance, such as a close icon button, within a side sheet.
checks.condition: For every side sheet, regardless of variant.

sourceHistory.summary: Accessibility guidance strengthens the visual guideline to a required close affordance.

evidence.result: Every rendered sheet variant includes the labeled close button within the content header.

checks.statement: Tab should move focus to non-disabled icon buttons; Space or Enter should activate a focused non-disabled icon button.
checks.condition: When keyboard or switch-control users navigate side-sheet icon buttons.

sourceHistory.summary: Keyboard table maps Tab and activation keys to non-disabled icon buttons.

evidence.result: The close control is a native button and remains in normal sequential keyboard focus order; Enter/Space activation is provided by native button semantics.

checks.statement: Expose the side sheet with the Dialog accessibility role.
checks.condition: When presenting a side sheet to assistive technology.

sourceHistory.summary: Labeling guidance assigns the Dialog role.

evidence.result: Modal side sheets use a native dialog, while standard sheets use a section with role=region; the source does not distinguish modal/non-modal role requirements.

implementation.notes: Only modal dialog semantics are established; applying Dialog to standard side sheets conflicts with the current non-modal region.
